new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record. Language not in the catalog and no existing statement; this source establishes Mulao as tonal (8 tone categories) with no word-stress rule stated, only unstressed toneless particles/reduced syllables and sentence-level emphatic stress.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Mulao (Dayin dialect) is described as a tone language: eight tone categories (six on unchecked syllables, two on checked syllables, the checked tones each split by vowel length), with tone conditioned by initial type and syllable type. The grammar has no word-stress or accent section and states no rule for where stress falls in a word. Its only stress remarks are (a) that some discourse/grammatical and sentence particles are unstressed and carry no fixed tone (their pitch follows sentence intonation), (b) that the vowel [ə] occurs in Chinese loans and in a small number of unstressed (reduced) syllables such as kə5 < kyo3 in kə5 lau5, and the numeral 'ten' may reduce to an unstressed form inside compound numerals, and (c) sentence-level emphatic/'logical' stress: certain adverbs (ja6 'also', naŋ1 'still', si 'yes') change meaning according to whether they are stressed, and the prominent part of an exclamatory sentence receives logical stress. Nothing on lexical or fixed word stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Unstressed toneless particles (lə, lɔ, a, yɔ, mə, pa, nɛ, kɔ etc.); [ə] in a few unstressed syllables; unstressed variant of səp 'ten' in compound numerals; weak forms si/sa of the conjunction 'or'; stressed vs unstressed readings of adverbs ja6, naŋ1 (sentence-level emphasis). No dialect said to differ in stress; Long'an dialect differs in tone pitch values and loan phonology only.
new_statements.identity_note: The phonology (inventory, Table 1 tone values 42/121/53/24/44/11; 55~42/12~11) is that of the Dayin dialect, Dongmen, Luocheng County, Guangxi (the initials list is headed 'Shang Nan'an Commune in Dongman [Dongmen] District, Luocheng County'); the authors say Mulao has no substantial dialect differences except Long'an (north Luocheng), which differs in tone pitch and takes its loan phonology from Cantonese rather than Southwestern Mandarin.
